articles.body: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge. "The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention." For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender. The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens. "Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them." Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns. "People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election." Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.
articles.headline: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon

articles.body: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Rafe Pilling, Director of Threat Intelligence in the Sophos Counter Threat Unit (CTU). How can a minor cyber intrusion disrupt food supplies, expose the weaknesses of industrial infrastructure and become an instrument of geopolitical confrontation? The cyberattacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems in France offer a revealing illustration of how digital vulnerabilities can translate into tangible economic disruption and potentially broader threats to society. As Pilling explains, “With a small amount of effort from the adversary side, they can create a large impact, in this case destroying food and producing empty shelves or empty refrigeration units in stores.” This asymmetry lies at the heart of contemporary cyber conflict, in which modest technical interventions can produce disproportionate economic and operational consequences

articles.body: Maryland Gov. Wes Moore said Democrats should work toward bipartisan deals, including on immigration, with Stephen Miller — despite the “well of distrust” he holds for the new White House chief of staff. Moore, a potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, told POLITICO’s Alex Burns on Tuesday that even though Miller is “the architect of some of the most racist, xenophobic, homophobic policies that we have,” he still believes there’s room to negotiate with the White House to ease the targeting of unauthorized immigrants living in the U.S. “One thing I've always said to the people of my state is I will work with anybody, I will bow to nobody,” he said at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s B20 Summit. “I wish that there was a different team, because I think the well of distrust that Stephen Miller and his policies have fostered have been deeply poisonous,” the governor continued. “But I still want to make sure that we're doing good things on behalf of the people of our jurisdictions, and I do think we have a window to do it.” President Donald Trump floated the possibility of a bipartisan immigration deal during a “60 Minutes” interview on Sunday as he acknowledged that the aggressive deportation policies he enacted at the beginning of his term were “too tough” and “took people that had good jobs.” Trump appeared to reverse course on Monday , telling reporters he opposed offering “amnesty” for undocumented immigrants. Voters have long said Trump’s mass deportation campaign is too aggressive, and some Hill Republicans have pointed the blame at Miller, who masterminded the policy, for their lost support among Hispanics this midterm cycle. Moore said there’s a window for “real bipartisan agreement” on immigration despite Miller’s ascension last week. Oklahoma GOP Gov. Kevin Stitt, who co-chairs the National Governors Association with Moore and also spoke at the summit, said Trump “won on a strong border” — but governors need a “seat at the table” when it comes to issuing workforce permits. Asked what message it sends to international business to have a top staffer in the White House who is a hardliner on immigration, Stitt deflected. “I'm not going to speak to his hardlineness on that issue,” Stitt said, referring to Miller. He added that he thinks there’s a path forward for unauthorized immigrants contributing to the economy: “If you are here chasing the American dream, contributing to society, and you've come here illegally and a company is vouching for you, that's literally what we want. We educate people here, we want the best and brightest here, and I think there's a solution.” Stitt, who has not spoken to Trump since the midterms, said the president has "softened" on immigration in recent interviews. “There's a real solution, and I think President Trump can lead on it. He can lead and hopefully ... the Democrat majority in the House and the Senate will now work with him and we can get something done,” the Republican governor said. Moore, in the interview, also pointed to AI safety as an area for potential bipartisan agreement and urged the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress to create federal regulations on AI companies that include “protections on our pocketbooks” along with protections for workforce development and infrastructure. So far, much of the regulation has been left to the states. But Democrats in Congress are weighing multiple bills to enact safety standards protecting consumers from AI as Americans grow increasingly concerned about the dangers of the technology. “It’s not useful to have 50 different guidelines for how this country should think about this,” Moore said. “We need Washington to get in the game.” The Democrat also warned businesses to stay away from Trump’s ballroom and meme coin. "I would tell you right now that this will not age well,” Moore told the audience at the B20 summit. “There will not be a long term benefit to this. That with the American people, the best way for us to fight for capitalism is to make sure that we're building a system that everyone can see the benefit for and that we're not parsing off who it can actually benefit." Andrew Howard contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Wes Moore wants immigration reform. Can he work with Stephen Miller?

articles.body: Democrats who just triumphed in a number of battlegrounds are facing pressure to make their states just a little less powerful in the fight for the presidency. The party’s sweeping victories present an opportunity for Democrats in states with newly won trifectas to join the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, an agreement between states to make sure whoever wins national popular vote becomes president by awarding their Electoral College votes to that winner, rather than the winner of the most votes in their state. The compact would go into effect when it’s enacted in states whose combined electoral vote total is at least 270. Currently, 18 historically blue states and Washington D.C. have joined the compact, a two-decade-long, nonpartisan project, with a combined 222 electoral votes. That means if Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin join, along with either Arizona or Nevada, the compact would go into effect in every member state, making it possible for the next president to be elected by winning the popular vote while losing the Electoral College. All five states will now be under unified Democratic control starting next year. Democrats in those five states, which will likely be battlegrounds in 2028 under the current system, have supported switching to national popular vote in the past. But it’s unclear whether they will move forward on national popular vote after gaining historic trifectas on the back of promising to lower costs for voters — a move that would make their own states less crucial for the 2028 presidential battle. Incoming Arizona Senate Majority Leader Priya Sundareshan told POLITICO her caucus will take up the national popular vote, but the timing remains unsettled. Sundareshan added she hasn’t spoken to Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs about national popular vote. Hobbs’ office declined to comment. “We certainly are and have been prepared to join the compact, and we also want to make sure that we are showing that our priorities are reflective of what we really focused on on the campaign trail,” she said. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro told POLITICO he is “open” to signing his state into the compact but suggested he hasn’t yet coordinated with state legislators on how national popular vote fits in with the rest of his agenda. He said separately Saturday at Crooked Media’s “Crooked Con” that the national popular vote “makes sense” and pledged to work with lawmakers “to figure out what the right mechanism going forward on that.” Some state leaders say they know they’d draw challenges and political fury if they attempt to rewrite the nation’s rules for electing presidents. Incoming Michigan Senate Majority Leader Darrin Camilleri said he’s open to enacting a national popular vote, but conceded that any change would likely invite lawsuits from Republicans. “Other states that have done this are not going to be the tipping-point states. We very well could be one of those tipping point-states, and so I want to ensure that everybody is on the same page,” Camilleri said. Michigan Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson’s representatives did not respond to a request for comment. Wisconsin Gov.-elect David Crowley previously backed a 2019 bill to have Wisconsin join the compact. When asked if he would do so as governor, Crowley said in a statement he “is focused on assembling an experienced transition team so his administration can be ready on day one to deliver results for working families across the Badger State.” Ben Wikler, the former Wisconsin Democratic Party chair and national popular vote advocate, dismissed concerns about battleground states diminishing their prominence in presidential elections, even as he acknowledged that “battleground states passing the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact is like the popular kids abolishing the concept of popularity.” “I've spoken to audiences all over the state of Wisconsin,” Wikler said. “Everyone here agrees that Wisconsinites shouldn't be high and mighty, lording over the powerless voters in the coastal states. We should be a one-person, one-vote democracy.” When Nevada Democrats held a trifecta in 2019, they put a bill to join the compact on former Gov. Steve Sisolak’s desk, but Sisolak vetoed it out of concern it would diminish the role of smaller states like Nevada in the electoral process. Nevada Gov.-elect Aaron Ford’s office declined to comment. Despite the uncertainty, the outside groups pushing the compact are optimistic enough states will join to trigger the compact ahead of the 2028 election. “I’ve never been more confident in my life,” said Patrick Rosenstiel, a spokesperson for National Popular Vote, the bipartisan group behind the compact.
articles.headline: Democrats plot their course on national popular vote

articles.body: The 2028 presidential race is already playing out in the text threads and phone calls of a new set of Democratic power brokers. A number of would-be White House contenders — including former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, former Ambassador Rahm Emanuel and Sens. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) and Cory Booker (D-N.J.) — have already reached out to various winners, interviews with rumored 2028 hopefuls and newly elected Democrats reveal. Incoming Reps. Nancy Lacore (D-S.C.) and Teresa Benitez-Thompson (D-Nev.), incoming Sens. Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Chris Pappas in New Hampshire and Annie Andrews in South Carolina, and New Mexico Gov.-elect Deb Haaland all got calls. The outreach signals a desire among Democrats who surfed a massive blue wave to victory last week to leverage those wins and influence the coming presidential contest, both in key early primary states and battlegrounds. "Lots of congratulatory calls with 'we would like to have conversations soon,'" said Morgan Jackson, a senior adviser to Sen.-elect Roy Cooper in North Carolina. Some newly elected Democrats are openly positioning themselves as kingmakers on the road to 2028, arguing their campaigns offer templates for the next crop of White House aspirants. Others are positioning themselves as ambassadors to their states. El-Sayed wants his party's next presidential nominee to support passing progressive policies like Medicare for All — and told POLITICO he hopes they’ll agree with his unflinching criticism of U.S. military support for Israel. Incoming Michigan Rep. William Lawrence said that Democrats won a “clear mandate” to take on Big Tech, including data centers , and to prevent endless wars, and he wants those issues to stay on “top of the agenda for 2028.” Haaland told POLITICO ahead of Election Day she wants Democrats to "have a plan for Indian tribes." Their rise will influence the potential 2028 field’s ability to navigate new geography and new demands while courting established kingmakers and party leaders. And some warning signs are already emerging: Allies of Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's are knives out for Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear , who they argue didn't do enough to help her as chair of the Democratic Governors Association and doesn't understand the power of Latino voters — a necessary component of any 2028 bid. First stop: South Carolina No state will be as central as South Carolina, which will go first on Democrats' presidential primary calendar and where the bench of candidates will be deepest. Longtime Democratic Rep. Jim Clyburn (S.C.) is still expected to reprise his role as the host and kingmaker . But Andrews’ and Lacore’s massive upsets last Tuesday have supercharged Democrats’ delegation in the state. Andrews has fielded multiple calls from potential presidential candidates since Election Day, according to a person with direct knowledge of her conversations. Lacore, too, has taken “many” congratulatory calls from potential Democratic candidates, per another person with direct knowledge. Sens. Raphael Warnock of Georgia and Kelly both campaigned for Andrews during the race, and Buttigieg and Beshear made appearances with Lacore in her coastal district. Clyburn has long been vocal about the direction of the Democratic Party, active on the trail and open with his endorsements and advice to presidential hopefuls — and just recently with POLITICO . It’s not clear how the two newcomers will seek to shape 2028: Representatives for both campaigns declined to comment. But Andrews, a pediatrician, made health care a central part of her campaign. And Lacore’s focus on veterans’ issues and national security could bring those to the forefront. The two of them and Clyburn are set to meet on Capitol Hill for the first time as South Carolina’s incoming delegation on Wednesday to plan how best to work together in Congress, according to a person familiar with the gathering. Antjuan Seawright, a Clyburn adviser and Democratic strategist, said the three Palmetto State Democrats will likely have “different” approaches to their involvement in the 2028 primary. “The three of them, individually and collectively, will have a tremendous opportunity to entertain and introduce South Carolina to the potential candidates who are seeking the office,” Seawright said. Kicking the tires in New Hampshire New Hampshire’s elected Democrats have long wielded outsize influence over the party’s nominating process in what was the first-in-the-nation primary state. Pappas, a four-term representative, and Rep.-elect Stefany Shaheen, the daughter of two longtime New Hampshire Democratic power players, are well steeped in 2028 after multiple potential candidates campaigned with them through the fall to gain footholds in the state. Pappas started signaling his status as a power broker in the final days of the election, and was on Kelly’s list of election-night phone calls. “We had a lot of visitors at the end of this campaign, maybe some folks who were just using me as an excuse to come visit New Hampshire and kick the tires a little bit,” Pappas said on WMUR in a post-election interview. Pappas told POLITICO on Monday he would “certainly” serve as an ambassador for candidates — and suggested there are “people who want to certainly come back soon. I think it’s going to kick off pretty quickly.” Jim Demers, a veteran Democratic strategist and liaison for presidential hopefuls in the state, told POLITICO he believes both Pappas and Shaheen could serve as key conduits for candidates looking to play in New Hampshire. “Both of them are very campaign smart, and so their advice to any of the potential presidential candidates will be important,” Demers said. “I would expect they’re going to be extremely popular and can be a big help to any of them who want help.” The progressive agenda in Michigan Michigan is already the epicenter of the Democratic Party’s most polarizing fights over policy and ideology. Now, the perennial battleground sits fifth in the presidential primary lineup. Few have been so openly positioning themselves to join the ranks of the state’s power brokers as El-Sayed, who declared even before his primary win that he would “dog” presidential hopefuls “up and down the state” to embrace his progressive platform, including Medicare for All. “It’s important to me that I've got a governing partner,” El-Sayed told POLITICO in a post-election interview. “I'm going to do what I can to make sure that I get one.” El-Sayed could play a significant role in shaping the debate over Israel in a state that gave rise to the “uncommitted” movement in 2024 — and where he ran aggressively against U.S. military aid to the country. The senator-elect said he hopes the next nominee will share his stance; when asked about that remark, Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he looks forward to “having a thoughtful conversation with” El-Sayed on the topic. “I will be advocating for what I believe to be right, and clearly my state agrees with me on this issue,” El-Sayed said, adding, “If you want to be where the voters are — if you want to be on the side of peace and on the side of justice and transparency — I believe that that is around holding Israel accountable to its war crimes and on making sure our tax dollars get used to do good things here rather than bad things somewhere else.” Others are ready to engage with their party’s future in a more neutral role. Jocelyn Benson, the moderate incoming governor, said in an interview that she will “certainly invite folks to come to our state to make their case to our residents.” Over in the West The West will have its biggest role in the calendar yet, with New Mexico joining Nevada as early calendar stops. As Nevada’s new top official with strong working-class appeal , Democratic Gov.-elect Aaron Ford could play a major role in shepherding 2028 candidates — should he choose to. He’s already fielded congratulatory calls from Moore, who leads the National Governors Association, and others. Benitez-Thompson, who will represent the large swath of rural northern Nevada, is already embracing her role as an ambassador for the region and has taken calls from a “number” of likely presidential contenders in the days after the midterm election. “I am dead set on making sure that I can bring resources home for northern Nevada and investments home into northern Nevada. I'll be talking to any and everyone who can help me move resources and levers to make that happen,” she said in an interview. "Come to northern Nevada, step off of the plane, but be ready for me to show you what our needs are." Adam Wren, Ali Bianco, Lauren Fedor, Aaron Pellish and Meredith Lee Hill contributed to this report.

articles.body: A former business partner is accusing MAGA media guru Alex Bruesewitz of receiving lavish gifts from foreign individuals in Qatar and Syria while also pursuing lucrative deals with other entities looking to unlock access to U.S. government officials. The allegations were made in a court filing Monday by Derek Utley, who co-founded the digital firm X Strategies in 2017 with Bruesewitz. Bruesewitz is a top outside adviser to President Donald Trump , having helped shape his 2024 campaign’s digital strategy, and X Strategies maintains the Trump War Room and Team Trump accounts on X. The company sued Utley in September , alleging he embezzled and gambled away millions of dollars from the firm. In the Monday filing responding to that lawsuit, Utley calls it a “marketing ploy masquerading as a federal lawsuit” and denies allegations he embezzled the company’s money or used its funds to gamble. The filing includes a countersuit against X Strategies that claims Utley was fired from the company without cause over a requested medical leave. (The firm’s original lawsuit had claimed Utley submitted “fake medical records” to "fraudulently" get six months paid leave, and was then fired.) Utley doesn’t explicitly accuse Bruesewitz of offering foreign officials political access in exchange for payments, but charges that Bruesewitz “pursued substantial business and financial relationships with foreign individuals, investors, and governmental representatives, including persons associated with Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, and Syria” while concealing those relationships. The filing does not include documentation to support its allegations. “The relationships and access Bruesewitz cultivated through X Strategies were valuable commercial assets, particularly to foreign interests seeking introductions to American political figures, access to governmental institutions, or assistance advancing their commercial and political objectives,” the filing says. “Upon information and belief, Bruesewitz received approximately $500,000 from individuals associated with Qatar in connection with an undisclosed business or consulting arrangement.” Bruesewitz’s lawyer Bradford Cohen denied all the allegations. “These are things that would be defamatory if made outside the four corners of the complaint,” Cohen said Monday evening, vowing to "vigorously" defend against the allegations. “We're asserting that everything in his factual allegations is either untrue, exaggerated, or completely fabricated,” he said. “Desperate men resort to desperate things, and this screams of desperation.” Bruesewitz continues to advise conservative figures in Trump’s orbit. He also leveraged his relationships with foreign officials when the war with Iran broke out to help charter a flight back to the U.S. for himself and other Americans who were stranded in Qatar, according to his social media posts at the time. Utley did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither did the White House. In another example, Utley claims Bruesewitz sought to charge an annual advisory fee of $1 million to a “Copenhagen-based investment firm with holdings in the United States and Europe.” The proposed deal, the filing said, included services like “providing access to American governmental officials, federal agencies, and financial institutions.” “These circumstances raise questions concerning potential registration and disclosure obligations under FARA,” the court filing says, referencing the Foreign Agents Registration Act, which requires public disclosures from those involved in lobbying or other activities representing foreign interests. Additionally, the filing alleges that Bruesewitz told Utley that his honeymoon hotel stay in the Maldives was paid for by “two Syrian billionaires” who provided access to a suite that ordinarily costs $15,000 a night. Bruesewitz has previously advocated for conservative influencers to disclose their relationships with foreign governments seeking to sway the Trump administration. He also said during a June interview with Tucker Carlson that he does not take any foreign payments. “Getting foreign influence out of the political ecosystem, specifically online, is a very — it’s a passion project of mine,” Bruesewitz said in the interview. “You can only imagine the type of money that these countries and other companies have tried to throw at me. I do not take any foreign money. I don’t take any money from the Gulf countries. I don't take any money from India. I don't take any money from Russia, China. No foreign countries.”
articles.headline: Court filing alleges Trump adviser received cash, luxury gifts from foreign interests

articles.body: Democrats’ blue wave blew up the 2028 battle map. But Josh Shapiro insists Texas isn’t going to replace Pennsylvania as the “ultimate swing state.” He needs it to be true. Shapiro’s theory of the case for 2028 has long rested on his ability to win resoundingly and repeatedly in what has recently been the nation’s biggest battleground state. On Tuesday, he helped deliver Democrats four congressional flips and their first trifecta in Harrisburg in three decades, all while running up a more than 20-point margin in his own reelection bid. He plowed over $10 million into state Democrats’ campaign arms and helped recruit and cut ads for candidates across House and state Senate races. He also flipped 11 counties President Donald Trump won in 2024 and, his team argued in a post-election memo shared first with POLITICO, showed “unique strength” with voters skeptical of the Democratic Party. It’s a significant show of force even in a wave election — one that could springboard him into a presidential bid if he chooses, even as Democrats turn their attention to redder turf . “The common-sense approach we’ve taken to governing, the kind of candidates we recruited to run for Congress who won, I think that that can be a model for our party,” Shapiro told POLITICO by phone late last week. And “it’s going to be important that we share our Pennsylvania model from what I would maintain … is still the ultimate swing state.” Shapiro continues to play coy about his presidential ambitions . He phoned Democrats’ primary kingmaker, Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C.) , after the election, but declined to discuss the details. When POLITICO asked Shapiro his timeline to decide a 2028 run, he replied: “I just wrapped up a meeting with the legislative leaders and my senior team to work on our agenda going forward, and that's what I'm focused on right now.” Here’s more from POLITICO’s chat with Shapiro, edited and condensed for length. You’ve got your trifecta. What’s your No. 1 priority? The first bill that will reach my desk will be to raise the minimum wage to 15 bucks an hour. I've been able to get a lot of stuff done through the Republican Legislature, but that's an example of something that hasn't. Is signing onto the National Popular Vote Compact something you’d be interested in? I have said that I am open to that, I think I’ve voiced some positivity toward it. As it relates to the trifecta, though, the leaders and I agreed that we would speak with one voice in announcing our initial agenda. A lot of Democrats are saying the biggest message that they got out of this wave election was the economy. Do you think that that's the biggest takeaway? I think in part that is correct, and that's why the first new law I want to pass in Pennsylvania is to put more money in people's pockets. I also think there was something deeper. … Substantively the issue that obviously mattered most was the high cost of everything; I think underneath that was a real fear that people had about the direction this country was going in, and they wanted to use their power to change it. Do you think the path to the presidency is moving out of the Blue Wall and into states like Texas, into the Sun Belt? Democrats are proving that we can win everywhere. … We added back to the Blue Wall. Ohio, with Amy [Acton]'s incredible victory there. I was proud to campaign for her. We’re showing we can win in these southern states. So I think the takeaway from Tuesday night is the map got a whole lot bigger for Democrats. And so long as Republicans continue to follow Trump and [Vice President JD] Vance off the cliff, their map is getting much smaller. Do you think that Texas will take over from Pennsylvania as the nation's biggest swing state? I mean, they're a big state, and they were just won by two outstanding Democrats. I was so impressed with both of them and how they ran their campaigns. And I imagine Texas is going to have a lot to say about the future leadership in our country. But not necessarily taking over Pennsylvania’s spot — I mean, come on. I’m Pennsylvania first. You’re never going to get me to come off of Pennsylvania being the ultimate swing state. Abdul El-Sayed told me he hopes the next Democratic presidential nominee shares his views on Israel. He opposes military aid to Israel. Do you agree that that's the stance the nominee, whoever it is, should take? Well, he is one voice in our party. And I look forward to getting a chance to talk to him and learn more about how he really thinks and how he really views these issues, and having a thoughtful conversation with him. Is there anyone coming out of Tuesday who you want to talk to, who you think ‘that person has a good message for the party’? I've talked to probably more than 20 people across the country since Tuesday night who won races at all levels. I've been incredibly impressed by the talent that chose to run for office and won in really tough states. I think I can learn from a lot of them, and I want to learn from them, and I want to listen to them, and I salute their victories. articles.body: A new Republican group thinks their party is too old, too moderate and too weak. So they’re launching an effort to replace the outgoing generation of politicians with a younger crop of America First-aligned lawmakers. American Ascent launches Monday with an eye toward building a bench of young conservatives that could flip some of the dozens of congressional seats that will be held by aging lawmakers in 2028. The 501(c)(4) will be run by Ryan Neuhaus, the former Heritage Foundation chief of staff. Its partners include an array of new-right allies of Vice President JD Vance, including Turning Point Action, which has already endorsed Vance for president in 2028, as well as the conservative think tank Claremont Institute and the watchdog group Oversight Project. A PAC that has backed challenges to other GOP incumbents led by Andy Surabian, a longtime aide to both Vance and Donald Trump Jr., will also partner closely with the effort. The effort was in the works before last week’s GOP washout. Still, its leaders say those results show Republicans must double down rather than shrink back from an aggressive populist agenda on issues from immigration to the economy. “For too long, the Republican Party has relied on rerunning candidates over and over again,” Neuhaus said. “The American people told us pretty clearly that they want to see younger, more energetic politicians leading in America, representing them. They want to feel closely connected to them, and American Ascent is going to accomplish that.” When asked if their recruits would primary incumbent Republicans, Neuhaus demurred. “That's up to them,” he said, referring to the candidates. “But I'll prepare any young and able and competent American to run for higher office.” Neuhaus is the former Heritage Foundation chief of staff who shouldered the blame for Kevin Roberts’ controversial video defending Tucker Carlson last year, after the podcaster hosted a friendly interview with white nationalist Nick Fuentes. He pointed to the 42-year-old Vance, Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas), Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.) and Rep.-elect Jace Yarbrough (R-Texas) as Republicans who are "inspirational to the base.” The organization will scout young conservative leaders and enroll them in a leadership training program called the “Fellowship for American Ascent.” The group has also compiled data suggesting the best opportunities to flip House, Senate and governors’ seats in 2028, based on candidate age, whether they plan to seek reelection, fundraising history and other factors. While the new organization is not affiliated with Vance — Neuhaus was adamant it is not a “Vance political project” — the effort parallels the new-right conservatism championed by the vice president. The American Leadership PAC, led by Surabian, a key political adviser to Vance, will operate in tandem with American Ascent, Neuhaus said. The PAC helped defeat anti-redistricting Republicans in Indiana's statehouse earlier this year. Surabian’s PAC will focus on open seats in safe red districts, a person familiar with the group’s plans said. Surabian did not return a request for comment. The effort is being bankrolled by an initial $12 million by GOP megadonor Thomas Klingenstein, the septuagenarian chair of the Claremont Institute’s board of directors and a major donor to Surabian’s American Leadership PAC as well as Trump-aligned Club for Growth and the socially conservative American Principles Project. Klingenstein has long argued that a “cold civil war” is underway in the U.S. between conservatives and their opponents. “America needs statesmen who understand we are fighting against an enemy that wants to destroy us,” Klingenstein said in a statement to POLITICO. “Our statesmen must understand in such a situation reaching across the aisle is a sucker’s game. American Ascent shall find such leaders and then develop them.” This new initiative’s organizers want to see a Republican Party aligned to the conservatism that Vance, a close ally of the Claremont Institute , has come to represent. They argue that today’s elected Republicans are largely out of touch with the economic needs of young Americans, and like Vance , blame the Iran war for much of the GOP’s current political problems. “[Tuesday] was a cataclysmic loss for Republicans,” said Noah Wall, whose State Leadership Initiative will help scout future candidates as part of the effort. “If we want a resurgence, you need strong, bold leaders. … Quite literally the biggest opportunity in history of the Republican Party of the modern era is what we're going to be going through over the next two years.” They also argue that mass deportations are a key motivator for young voters, not a deterrent. “Republicans lost on the economy. They did not lose on the immigration agenda, which voters time and time again say is the number one best issue for Republicans to run on,” said Bradley Devlin, the former Daily Signal editor who will lead American Ascent’s communications, pointing to exit polling that showed immigration as a major motivator for Republicans. Republicans face a serious problem with young voters and Latino voters , who both shifted hard to the left in last week’s midterms. Voters ages 18-29 backed Democrats 70% to 28% — a 33-point shift from 2024, per the New York Times’ data . A September POLITICO Poll found that nearly one-third of non-MAGA Republicans said that Trump’s deportation push has been “too aggressive.” Vance’s office did not return a request for comment. “We watched a complete rebuke of the type of Republicans that were in Congress. Old ideas are for old people,” said Jackson Hines, the nephew and former bodyman of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who joins the organization as vice president. The key to resolving the GOP’s malaise, supporters say, is recruiting strong, young candidates who are true believers on populist economics and a staunch America First foreign policy. “[Young voters] liked what was promised on the campaign trail in 2024 — no new wars, mass deportation, end of corruption in government — and they still want those things,” said Mike Howell, president of the Oversight Project, who will partner with Klingenstein’s new group. “And so we need to have people committed to doing them in positions of power.”

Bajo este despectivo apelativo, los ultras englobaban a sus enemigos: musulmanes, judíos, inmigrantes, antifascistas y colectivos vulnerables, según los chats intervenidos por la Policía Nacional a los que ha tenido acceso EL PAÍS. Los mensajes forman parte de la investigación que desarrolla el Juzgado de Instrucción número 1 de Gijón y recogen las comunicaciones en las que los ultras planean acciones violentas contra mezquitas, sinagogas y centros de menores no acompañados. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-11/nucleo-nacional-planeo-atacar-mezquitas-y-sinagogas-hay-que-empezar-con-las-incineraciones.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Vivían puerta con puerta, pero no sabían su nombre. Cuando a primera hora del miércoles los furgones policiales cortaron la calle, los vecinos de la localidad de Montijo (15.195 habitantes, Badajoz) intuyeron que el operativo iba a la casa de fachada ocre y molduras destartaladas. Acertaron. Presintieron también que el registro tenía algo que ver con el tráfico de drogas. Que se equivocaban lo supieron cuando, como les ordenaron los agentes, regresaron a sus domicilios y la noticia de lo que ocurría en ese instante al otro lado de la calle les estalló en sus teléfonos. “Desarticulan una red criminal de tráfico y compraventa de bebés”. Una sinfonía de notificaciones, de titulares perturbadores que comenzaron a darle dimensiones pesadillescas a lo que pasaba en la casa de su vecina sin nombre. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-11/los-interrogantes-de-la-operacion-luna-que-se-sabe-y-que-no-sobre-la-presunta-venta-de-menores.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>Hacía falta un gran templo para acoger a los familiares (cerca de 150) de las 69 víctimas del accidente ferroviario de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/nena-dime-algo-el-ultimo-mensaje-del-marido-de-una-victima-de-urda.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/nena-dime-algo-el-ultimo-mensaje-del-marido-de-una-victima-de-urda.html">Urda </a>(Toledo); a supervivientes heridos y a los profesionales de distintos uniformes que intervinieron en la emergencia; y, sin embargo, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-10/el-arzobispo-de-toledo-pide-en-el-funeral-de-las-victimas-del-tren-de-urda-que-se-asuman-responsabilidades-y-se-repare-en-justicia.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-10/el-arzobispo-de-toledo-pide-en-el-funeral-de-las-victimas-del-tren-de-urda-que-se-asuman-responsabilidades-y-se-repare-en-justicia.html">en la catedral de Toledo este martes no cabía tanto dolor.</a> El funeral sirvió para recordar, en medio de las polémicas y miserias de la precampaña electoral, que el tiempo se detuvo hace apenas 15 días para decenas de padres, hijos, hermanos, parejas y amigos de los pasajeros de los trenes siniestrados en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. También para poner de manifiesto la frivolidad de algunas manifestaciones recientes, como darse golpes en el pecho para celebrar en un mitin la dimisión de un compañero o hacer juegos de palabras con el nombre de un ministro. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-10/el-dolor-no-cabia-en-la-catedral-de-toledo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El dolor no cabía en la catedral de Toledo

articles.body: <p>La Catedral de Toledo ha acogido este martes el funeral por los 69 fallecidos en el accidente de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/nena-dime-algo-el-ultimo-mensaje-del-marido-de-una-victima-de-urda.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/nena-dime-algo-el-ultimo-mensaje-del-marido-de-una-victima-de-urda.html">Urda</a> del pasado 28 de octubre, y el arzobispo, en una homilía cariñosa hacia las víctimas y contundente hacia las autoridades, ha lanzado un claro mensaje: que se esclarezcan las causas del accidente, que se depuren responsabilidades y que se repare en justicia.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-10/el-arzobispo-de-toledo-pide-en-el-funeral-de-las-victimas-del-tren-de-urda-que-se-asuman-responsabilidades-y-se-repare-en-justicia.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

"></img><p>El juzgado de Vigilancia Penitenciaria de la Audiencia Nacional (AN) ha revocado el régimen de semilibertad concedido a <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/el-gobierno-vasco-vuelve-a-conceder-la-semilibertad-a-anboto-tras-rechazarla-un-juez-hace-cinco-meses.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-02/el-gobierno-vasco-vuelve-a-conceder-la-semilibertad-a-anboto-tras-rechazarla-un-juez-hace-cinco-meses.html">la exjefa de ETA Soledad Iparraguirre, alias <i>Anboto</i></a>, así como los terceros grados otorgados a los exdirigentes de la banda terrorista <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-20/la-fiscalia-se-opone-por-segunda-vez-a-ampliar-la-semilibertad-al-exjefe-de-eta-olarra-guridi.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-20/la-fiscalia-se-opone-por-segunda-vez-a-ampliar-la-semilibertad-al-exjefe-de-eta-olarra-guridi.html">Juan Antonio Olarra Guridi</a> y Arkaitz Aguirregabiria. articles.body: <p>El Gobierno ha decidido echar toda la carne en el asador en <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-19/el-gobierno-arranca-los-martes-sociales-con-un-decreto-para-mejorar-las-prestaciones-por-viudedad-incapacidad-para-victimas-del-terrorismo-y-de-violencia-de-genero.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-19/el-gobierno-arranca-los-martes-sociales-con-un-decreto-para-mejorar-las-prestaciones-por-viudedad-incapacidad-para-victimas-del-terrorismo-y-de-violencia-de-genero.html">políticas sociales y mensajes progresistas</a> en estas últimas tres semanas antes de las elecciones. El Ejecutivo hará dos consejos de ministros extraordinarios, este viernes y el próximo, además de los dos ordinarios que quedan los dos martes, según fuentes del Gobierno, porque las medidas que tiene que aprobar son tantas y tan diferentes que necesita dividirlas en cuatro. Además, así se garantiza ocupar más espacio mediático y generar más debate con sus iniciativas, que <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/un-precedente-con-muchas-y-radicales-dudas-es-constitucional-aprobar-los-decretos-de-vivienda-tras-la-disolucion-de-las-cortes.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/un-precedente-con-muchas-y-radicales-dudas-es-constitucional-aprobar-los-decretos-de-vivienda-tras-la-disolucion-de-las-cortes.html">tendrán que ser aprobadas en la Diputación Permanente.</a> El Ejecutivo solo ha dejado libre el último viernes antes de las elecciones, día del cierre de campaña. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-10/el-gobierno-multiplica-las-medidas-sociales-antes-de-las-elecciones-y-apoya-la-huelga-general.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: En la vigília de la vaga general de l’11-N, membres dels principals sindicats convocants han passat pel bàsics per fer una crida a la mobilització i la protesta . Enrique Rodríguez Ruiz , secretari d’Acció Sindical de CCOO de Catalunya; Òscar Riu , secretari de Política Sindical de la UGT de Catalunya, i Enric Aragonès , portaveu del Sindicat de Llogateres , han coincidit a dir que esperen un seguiment important de la vaga. Sobre l’aturada d’aquest dimecres, Enric Aragonès ha recordat que feia anys que planificaven aquesta vaga general i que l’han convocada quan han vist l’oportunitat de plantejar-la. Tot I això, ha avisat: “Passi el que passi el dia 29-N, vindran més vagues i més vagues de lloguers “. A més, ha advertit: “La lluita sindical queda en no res si els preus segueixen pujant sense control”. També et pot interessar Comerciants del passeig de Gràcia, abans de la vaga: “Ho vivim amb certa angoixa” Guillem González Claramunt 1 minut de lectura Els sindicats tradicionals apunten a la patronal Des de la UGT han recordat que el problema dels sous i l’augment del cost de la vida no és nou. “Nosaltres fa un any que diem a la patronal que hem de negociar un augment de salaris . Tenim la negociació col·lectiva aturada i la gent no arriba a final de mes”, ha apuntat Òscar Riu. Més enllà dels empresaris, CCOO ha buscat culpables en l’aritmètica del Congrés dels Diputats . Rodríguez Ruiz ha reconegut que el govern ha intentat fer coses, “no totes les que serien necessàries”, però que la correlació de forces amb PP, Vox i Junts ha fet que no hagin tirat endavant lleis que podrien haver contribuït que la situació no fos l’actual. articles.body: Barcelona viu aquest dimecres una jornada de vaga general , la primera que es convoca a l’estat espanyol des de fa 14 anys, és a dir, des del 2012. L’aturada es fa per dos motius principals, el dret a l’habitatge i la fi dels desnonaments i per reivindicar una millora de les condicions laborals i salarials . Tot i que la vaga està convocada pels sindicats majoritaris, CCOO i UGT , l’embrió de la protesta va néixer dins del moviment pel dret a l’habitatge arran del desnonament de la Maricarmen , de 87 anys, del seu pis a Madrid. La jornada de vaga arrenca a primera hora del matí amb mobilitzacions al carrer i piquets informatius a les empreses. A la tarda hi ha convocada una manifestació unitària que sortirà dels Jardinets de Gràcia, i una altra marxa alternativa que sortirà de la plaça de Jacint Verdaguer. Tot i això, aquest dimarts al vespre, ja hi ha hagut els primers piquets informatius a Mercabarna dels principals sindicats. Segueix en directe la vaga de l’11-N , amb totes les afectacions a la mobilitat, l’educació, la sanitat i a infraestructures clau com el port o l’aeroport.  També et pot interessar Manifestació per la vaga general de l’11 de novembre: horari, lloc i manifest Clara Aliaguilla 2 minuts de lectura

articles.body: (ACN) Un matrimoni de 60 anys en situació de vulnerabilitat té programat el desnonament del seu habitatge de renda antiga, a Gràcia, el dia de la vaga general . Segons han detallat fonts municipals, es tracta d’un cas d’uns inquilins que no disposen de contracte de lloguer, ja que qui hi figurava era un tiet difunt i hi residien des de feia gairebé 20 anys . La voluntat de la parella era subrogar el contracte , però les mateixes fonts han indicat que la propietat no ho ha acceptat i tampoc ha volgut negociar amb el Servei d’Intervenció i Mediació en Situacions de Pèrdua d’Habitatge i Ocupacions ( SIPHO ) perquè la família continués vivint al carrer de Fraternitat, número 24. També et pot interessar Barcelona acorda que no hi haurà desnonaments en aplicació del decret anticrisi del Govern espanyol Redacció 1 minut de lectura Rebuig a la subrogació Des de l’administració local han assenyalat que la propietat ha rebutjat la subrogació , ja que “no es preveuen les condicions previstes normativament, en ser un tiet l’antic titular”. D’altra banda, les mateixes fonts han explicat que la justícia ha argumentat la negativa de l’ajornament del llançament, d’acord amb el nou decret d’habitatge , aprovat a principis d’octubre, perquè en “aquest cas no s’hi aplica”. El matrimoni, un dels membres del qual té una discapacitat del 65 % , està vinculat al SIPHO i a l’ Oficina d’Habitatge de Gràcia . Alhora, es troba en procés per inscriure’s a la Mesa d’Emergència i està inscrit al registre de sol·licitants d’habitatge de protecció oficial de Barcelona (RSHPOB). Fonts del consistori han informat que no s’ha activat l’allotjament temporal d’urgència perquè té “suport de la xarxa familiar ”.
articles.headline: Un matrimoni vulnerable de 60 anys, en risc de ser desnonat el dia de la vaga d’habitatge

articles.body: Abans de ser utilitzada com a dita per referenciar ubicacions molt llunyanes, la quinta forca va existir de veritat. Era un dels cinc emplaçaments de l’antiga Barcelona on s’ajusticiava els criminals, és a dir, on se’ls penjava fins a la mort . La principal es trovaba a la zona de l’actual pla de Palau, i n’hi havia d’altres que estaven repartides en el territori intramuralles. La de Sant Antoni o la del Born eren de les més conegudes. La darrera de totes —o si més no, la més allunyada del centre de la ciutat— era aquesta cinquena forca, ubicada als terrenys on es troba ara la Trinitat Vella. Servia per marcar el límit jurisdiccional del Consell de Cent —òrgan rector de la ciutat durant l’edat mitjana— i alhora, prevenir els malfactors . “Si cometien crims, podien anticipar com acabarien”, explica l’historiador Joan Pallarès. La forca més llunyana Ubicada al collet de Finestrelles, aquesta forca es trobava en una de les portes d’entrada més concorregudes de Barcelona, la que connectava amb l’interior de Catalunya: “Per aquesta via hi venia la gent de Terrassa, Sabadell, Vic, Manresa, Berga…”, assenyala Pallarès. Ara bé, tot i senyalitzar l’arribada a la ciutat, aquesta forca continuava trobant-se molt lluny del nucli del municipi , gairebé a una hora i mitja de trajecte del terreny enmurallat. “En un temps en què les persones no estaven acostumades a viatjar, aquesta resultava una distància realment llunyana”, afegeix. Per això, segons explica la llegenda, la gent barcelonina va anar introduint dins del llenguatge popular les referències a la quinta forca per referir-se a ubicacions molt llunyanes. L’execució, un acte habitual Pallarès reconeix que avui dia tothom s’esgarrifaria en veure una execució a la forca, però recorda que durant l’edat mitjana aquesta mena d’actes eren molt normals. Uns espectacles que es van produir aproximadament des del segle VII fins ben entrat el XIX i que congregaven grans multituds : “En algunes execucions hi podia haver prop de 4.000 persones”. Si bé és cert que la majoria de forques eren punts d’execució de criminals, ni havia algunes que complien amb una altra funció, com la de la Trinitat: “En aquesta no s’executava persones, simplement s’hi penjaven membres esquarterats , com ara braços, cames o caps, de criminals ja morts”. Una creu amb història El punt exacte on es trobava la forca es desconeix. Això, però, no havia de ser motiu per no recordar aquest punt amb tanta història que, segons Pallarès, enorgulleix el veïnat de la Trinitat Vella. Per rememorar la forca es va decidir col·locar-hi una creu que també atesora un gran valor patrimonial per al districte de Sant Andreu. Es tracta d’una rèplica de la peça que des del segle XII va servir per senyalitzar els 30 passos de la parròquia de Sant Andreu de Palomar, és a dir, el terreny sacre que envoltava l’església de l’antic municipi i on no es podia cometre cap acte de violència . articles.headline: “Això és a la quinta forca”, una dita popular d’origen sinistre a la Trinitat Vella

articles.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha lliurat aquesta tarda les 25 Medalles d’Honor de la Ciutat d’aquest 2026 en un acte celebrat al Saló de Cent i presidit per l’alcalde, Jaume Collboni . Com cada any, cinc dels guardonats corresponen a l’àmbit de ciutat i 20 han estat triats pels 10 districtes. Les medalles distingeixen persones i entitats que hagin contribuït al desenvolupament de la consciència ciutadana i els valors cívics amb la pràctica de la seva labor professional o social. Cinc medalles de ciutat En la categoria ciutat , els guardons s’han donat a cinc personalitats de diferents àmbits social, artesanal i cultural de la ciutat. Una medalla ha reconegut l’activista i polític Juan de Dios Ramírez-Heredia per la tasca constant de defensa dels drets del poble gitano i la contribució a fer de Barcelona un referent en la lluita contra la discriminació. En l’esfera teatral, s’ha distingit l’actriu i directora Imma Colomer Marcet com a figura essencial del teatre català contemporani, coincidint amb el 50è aniversari del Teatre Lliure , del qual va ser fundadora. Una altra medalla s’ha atorgat a l’empresari i joier Joan Oliveras i Baguès per la seva contribució al patrimoni artístic i artesanal de la ciutat i a les seves institucions culturals. En l’àmbit artístic, s’ha reconegut l’artista Mari Chordà Recasens per la seva trajectòria artística multidisciplinària com a pintora, poeta i activista feminista. Pel que fa a la cinquena medalla s’ha concedit al professor i activista Isidre Gutiérrez de Tena en reconeixement de la seva trajectòria de compromís cívic i social especialment en el suport i l’acompanyament a persones en situació d’atur i vulnerabilitat. Durant l’acte de lliurament, l’alcalde, Jaume Collboni, ha destacat que els premiats representen la identitat de Barcelona . “Amb el vostres compromís cívic, heu aportat valor, essència, memòria i significat a la ciutat”, ha remarcat. També et pot interessar L’Andreuenc, L’Obrador dels 15 i l’Òptica Gantzer guanyen els Premis Barcelona Comerç 2026 Ester Magdaleno 2 minuts de lectura 20 medalles a proposta dels districtes Les 20 medalles proposades pels 10 districtes de Barcelona han distingit tant personalitats destacades del teixit veïnal, social i cultural dels barris, com també entitats i associacions. Els guardonats en aquest 2026 han estat les següents: Ciutat Vella Josep Lluís Esteras , el Iaio , per més de 50 anys dedicats a la comunitat i a la transmissió de les tradicions festives a través de l’Associació d’Amics dels Gegants del Pi. Agrupació de Comerciants i Industrials de la Barceloneta (ACIB) , pels més de 70 anys de defensa del comerç de proximitat, la gastronomia de qualitat i el teixit social d’aquest barri. L’Eixample Trini Capdevila i Burniol , en reconeixement de la seva participació activa en òrgans institucionals i comunitaris per fer de l’Eixample un espai més amable per al veïnat. Trapelles de Sant Antoni , per gairebé dues dècades dedicades a apropar la cultura popular i el món del foc a la canalla del barri. Les Corts Associació de Veïns de Sant Ramon Nonat , per la defensa del benestar col·lectiu i el foment d’un sentiment de pertinença al barri de la Maternitat i Sant Ramon. Jordi Lobo i Sastre , per la trajectòria en l’àmbit de l’educació especial, el moviment associatiu i la vida comunitària de les Corts i Pedralbes. Sarrià – Sant Gervasi Fundació TEAS , per la tasca d’inclusió social de persones adultes amb discapacitat intel·lectual i pluridiscapacitat a través de l’art i del treball psicocorporal. Lluís Amat , en reconeixement del seu compromís amb l’acció veïnal i l’esforç per a la millora de les condicions de vida dels veïns del barri de Pedralbes. També et pot interessar Ricky Rubio, els Verdi, el Vall d’Hebron i Pitu Abril, entre els Premis betevé 2026 Gabriela Grífol Porta 4 minuts de lectura Gràcia Conxita Casanovas , com a referent a Catalunya del periodisme i la crítica cinematogràfica i per la tasca de difusió i promoció del cinema. L’Independent de Gràcia , com a model de periodisme de proximitat que ha sabut explicar la realitat quotidiana del territori i donar veu a veïnat, entitats i iniciatives locals. Horta-Guinardó Robert Manrique Ripoll , en reconeixement d’una trajectòria vital de compromís, dignitat i servei als altres dedicada a la defensa de les víctimes del terrorisme. Montserrat Pujolar i Giménez , per una trajectòria artística i cultural marcada per la humanitat, el talent i el compromís amb la música catalana. Nou Barris Associació de Comerciants de Roquetes , per la tasca a favor del comerç de proximitat, la convivència, la seguretat i la vida de barri. Vocalia de Dones – Centre Cultural García Lorca , en reconeixement de la contribució al manteniment d’un teixit associatiu que ofereix xarxes de suport mutu entre dones de diferents orígens. Sant Andreu Joan Pallarés , per la seva intensa vinculació amb els barris de Sant Andreu i la Sagrera, que ha contribuït a teixir comunitat des d’àmbits diversos com l’espeleologia, la comunicació o la cultura. Fundació OSAS , per promoure una societat inclusiva i oferir serveis integrals a persones amb discapacitat intel·lectual, malaltia mental i trastorns de conducta. Sant Martí Taller d’Història del Clot – Camp de l’Arpa , pels 20 anys dedicats a la recerca i la divulgació de la història del barri del Clot. Carles Meilán , per la seva trajectòria professional orientada a l’educació, l’esport i el desenvolupament integral de les persones. articles.body: Les obres de transformació del recinte històric de la Fira de Montjuïc entren en una fase decisiva amb l’ enderroc del vell Palau de Congressos . La maquinària pesant ja treballa directament sobre l’estructura de l’edifici. Amb una gran pinça hidràulica s’han començat a enderrocar les parets laterals de l’edifici, una imatge necessària per donar pas a la construcció d’un recinte multifuncional , previst per a l’any 2029, el centenari de l’Exposició Internacional del 29. L’activitat a la fira és constant en diversos fronts aquesta tardor. Molt a prop del Palau de Congressos, les excavadores continuen amb la retirada de la runa del Pavelló 4 , que va començar a enderrocar-se al juliol i que actualment ja es troba completament a terra. Les màquines treballen per preparar l’espai on es construirà el futur palau multifuncional, obra dels arquitectes Smiljan Radic, Miquel Mariné Núñez, Beatriz Borque i César Rueda Bonet . Un palau nou de congressos i un altre de multifuncional Les obres, que es preveuen acabar a finals d’any, reaprofitaran el formigó enderrocat per a la construcció del palau multifuncional . Es tracta d’un conjunt monumental de 20.500 m² distribuïts en dues plantes , amb molta llum. Una estructura metàl·lica lleugera el dotarà de permeabilitat i una millor integració amb l’entorn. En paral·lel, ja estan també en marxa els treballs per remodelar el Palau d’Alfons XIII , que preservarà l’estructura original, dissenyada per Josep Puig i Cadafalch. Serà en aquest recinte on s’ubicarà el futur Palau de Congressos , un nou complex amb un gran auditori i un jardí de prop de 7.000 m². El Palau del Vestit es desvesteix també Les actuacions a la fira inclouen també la intervenció al Palau del Vestit , on ja han començat les tasques de la retirada de la coberta de fibrociment , pas previ a la demolició parcial de l’edifici. Les obres en conservaran la icònica porxada de columnes que dona a la plaça d’Espanya, mentre que la resta de l’estructura serà enderrocada. L’interior d’aquest palau es transformarà en un pol d’innovació estretament vinculat a la Fira de Montjuïc . A més, acollirà un equipament de 1.100 m² , amb espais d’ús veïnal per als barris de la Font de la Guatlla i Hostafrancs. També et pot interessar Què passa al teu barri? articles.body: El president de l’ Associació d’Amics del Passeig de Gràcia , Lluís Sans, ha explicat al bàsics, de betevé, com viuen els comerciants les hores prèvies a la vaga general de dimecres. Sans ha avisat que els aldarulls del mes d’octubre són un precedent i que viuen el que pugui passar després de la manifestació “amb certa angoixa “. Pel que fa al desplegament policial, els Amics del Passeig de Gràcia asseguren que tenen “el ferm compromís, tant dels Mossos d’Esquadra com de la Guàrdia Urbana de Barcelona, de protegir el centre de la ciutat “. Tot i això, Sans ha avançat que hi haurà comerços que tancaran abans d’hora de manera preventiva. “Estarem molt atents al que pugui passar”, ha resumit el president de l’associació. Sans creu que, a l’acampada, “ja no hi ha tants activistes, s’ha tornat un campament majoritàriament d’indigents “. Per això, reclama que el centre recuperi la normalitat i que hi hagi l’enllumenat de Nadal que hi ha cada any. articles.body: La tapa, un clàssic de la nostra gastronomia, normalment s’associa a bars i tavernes. On no és tan habitual trobar-ne és als hotels de luxe de Barcelona, però fins al 15 de novembre fer un platet en un cinc estrelles és possible. La desena edició de l’ Hotel Tapa Tour proposa una ruta gastronòmica per 12 hotels de cinc estrelles i cinc estrelles gran luxe de Barcelona amb la tapa de protagonista. Un any més l’objectiu és acostar la gastronomia hotelera al gran públic i reivindicar els hotels com a espais gastronòmics oberts de la ciutat. Per això, durant uns dies, els barcelonins poden descobrir restaurants, jardins i terrasses i tastar les propostes exclusives en format tapa per un preu entre els 8 i els 15 euros . Cada mossegada pretén condensar la personalitat, la creativitat i l’estil de la cuina de cada hotel. “L’Hotel Tapa Tour neix per trencar el gel, per perdre la por a entrar en aquests hotelassos que encara fan cert respecte i donar a conèixer els seus espais gastronòmics”, reivindica Nona Rubio, fundadora de l’Hotel Tapa Tour. Platets maridats amb DO Ribera del Duero i DO Cava A cada establiment hi haurà entre dues i quatre propostes que competiran pel Premi Tapa Aliments d’Espanya, i optaran a la gran final al Saló Gourmets 2027 a Madrid. Les dues categories del concurs són la tapa nacional amb vi DO Ribera del Duero i la tapa fusió amb cava DO Cava . També es podrà provar la croqueta d’autor amb cervesa o vermut i la tapa dolça amb un còctel amb alcohol o sense. La millor croqueta i tapa dolça es decidirà per votació popular. També et pot interessar L’agenda gastronòmica de novembre a Barcelona: tots els plans per als amants del bon menjar Aitana Molina 8 minuts de lectura Hotels i restaurants que se sumen a la ruta Aquest aparador de l’alta gastronomia hotelera ha incorporat dues de les obertures més recents a la ciutat. L’ Hotel Club 29 , que ha començat aquest setembre al passeig de Gràcia, 29-31, amaga el restaurant Els Cavalls, de cuina clàssica d’hotel catalana. El xef Pau Gascó presenta una tapa de caviar de la terra (consomé tradicional clarificat amb caviar de tòfona) i un platet d’ànec i blat de moro (arepa farcida d’ànec lacat a l’estil Pequín). Pel cuiner, els hotels com el Club 29 “són racons maquíssims que conviden a tenir un moment de luxe privat ” i anima els barcelonins a creuar les portes i descobrir aquest racó amagat de l’Eixample. Una altra novetat hotelera és el BLESS Barcelona , que ha començat l’aventura a la plaça de Catalunya, 10, aquest agost amb el restaurant Sinedie , de cuina mediterrània amb tocs italians. El xef Borja Hontoria ens convida a tastar una tapa de cocota de carxofa amb salsa verda de pernil i vel ibèric i un platet d’ arancini de cua de bou amb formatge pecorino. La iniciativa de la ruta gastronòmica els ha servit com a carta de presentació de la proposta gastronòmica del nou hotel a la ciutat. Aquests establiments no s’ho han pensat i s’han sumat a l’aventura amb altres restaurants ja consolidats com el Monument Hotel (passeig de Gràcia, 75) ubicat en un palauet modernista que va obrir el 2020. Aquí també tenen novetats, el restaurant Bera, que va engegar a l’abril amb el segell inconfusible del xef Martín Berasategui . Aquí els plats del cuiner basc es mengen en un format més informal, per compatir i més accessible. El xef executiu del Monument, Gabriele Milani , presenta dues tapes amb ADN de la casa. El tàrtar de vaca gallega amb esferificació d’oliva arbequina i el clàssic de la casa, biquini trufat amb botifarra del perol i scamorza fumada. Per Milani, aquesta és una oportunitat perquè la gent tasti platets nous amb bons vins i creu que “és divertit i aporta alguna cosa més a la ciutat de Barcelona”. També et pot interessar Barcelona perd una estrella Michelin: el restaurant Oria, de Martín Berasategui, tanca Aitana Molina 1 minut de lectura Tapes als grans hotels tot l’any Si vols fer una tapa en una de la desena d’hotels que participen en l’Hotel Tapa Tour ho pots fer a través de les tres rutes que proposa el festival o triar entre els establiments que hi participen: Hotel Club 29, Mandarin Oriental Barcelona, Renaissance Barcelona, Monument Hotel, Cotton House Hotel, El Palace Barcelona, Almanac Barcelona, NHC Collection Gran Hotel Calderón, BLESS Barcelona, Kimpton Vividora Barcelona, The Barcelona EDITION i Torre Melina Gran Meliá. Plenament consolidat, el festival vol fer un pas més i l’any vinent passarà a tenir una ruta permanent amb una selecció d’hotels que oferiran una tapa i maridatge durant tot l’any . Això sí, la cita amb la ruta gastronòmica tornarà a Barcelona al novembre. “Farem una selecció molt curada d’hotels amb una proposta gastronòmica interessant i amb espais bonics que vingui de gust visitar”, assenyala la fundadora de la iniciativa.

articles.body: (ACN) La presidenta actual del banc Santander , Ana Botín , ha anunciat que ella serà l’últim membre de la seva família que dirigeix l’entitat. Ho ha dit en una entrevista al diari Financial Times publicada aquest dimarts. “No hi haurà un altre Botín dirigint el Santander”, ha assegurat la presidenta, que és la quarta generació de la seva família que dirigeix l’entitat. “No voldria que cap dels meus fills treballés amb mi” Botín va assumir la presidència del banc el 2014, després de la mort sobtada del seu pare, Emilio Botín, que comandava la companyia financera. “No voldria que cap dels meus fills treballés amb mi perquè és molt dur”, ha expressat Ana Botín. El diari financer apunta que un possible escenari que s’està considerant és que el Santander dividís el rol de Botín en dues parts, per separar una presidència no executiva i donar més autoritat al director executiu , segons fonts coneixedores consultades pel mitjà britànic. articles.body: Amb motiu de la vaga general d’aquest 11 de novembre, la Generalitat ha decretat serveis mínims per garantir el funcionament del transport públic, l’educació o la sanitat. Tot i això, hi ha determinades franges horàries —en les quals habitualment hi ha menys afluència de viatgers— en què no està garantit el transport . Tampoc no hi ha serveis mínims decretats en el cas de l’educació secundària i el batxillerat . A continuació t’expliquem quins són els serveis que no estan garantits durant aquesta vaga. També et pot interessar Serveis mínims per la vaga general de l’11 de novembre al transport públic, educació i sanitat Emma Monrós Rosell 2 minuts de lectura Sense transport públic fora de les hores punta En el cas del transport públic, el govern ha decretat un serveis mínims del 25 % durant les hores punta , és a dir de 6.30 a 9.30 h i de 16.30 a 21 h. Fora d’aquestes franges no hi ha fixat un percentatge mínim de prestació de servei i dependrà de l’assistència de treballadors que decideixin no secundar la vaga. Aquesta situació afecta tant el metro com els autobusos de TMB, als Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat de Catalunya (FGC), el TRAM i la resta de transports urbans i interurbans. En el cas de Rodalies la restricció del servei és més severa, i no hi haurà servei de tren fora de les hores punta decretades per la Generalitat —de 6.30 a 9.30 h i de 16.30 a 21 h—, quan els serveis mínims seran també del 25 %. Tampoc no tenen assignats serveis mínims els transports d’oci com el Bus Turístic o el Telefèric de Montjuïc i, per tant, l’Ajuntament de Barcelona avisa que “no es pot garantir segur que funcionin”. Per contra, on sí que hi ha serveis mínims del 50 % durant tota la jornada és als autobusos que cobreixen el trajecte entre Barcelona i l’aeroport . També et pot interessar Vaga general: què passa si no pots arribar a la feina i ets servei mínim o vols treballar? Olga Borràs Boada 2 minuts de lectura Els instituts de secundària, sense serveis mínims En el cas de l’educació, el govern ha decretat uns serveis mínims d’un docent per cada sis classes a l’educació infantil i primària. En canvi, l’educació secundària no té assignats serveis mínims , i només s’obliga a treballar una persona de l’equip directiu per centre. Aquesta situació afecta tant els alumnes de l’ESO com també els que fan batxillerat . A les universitats públiques tampoc no hi ha serveis mínims assignats per la vaga general. Els centres recomanen al professorat no fer activitats avaluables (en alguns s’ha declarat una aturada acadèmica), i no fer activitats en què es tingui en compte la presencialitat dels estudiants. 25 % de la plantilla a l’atenció primària no urgent Pel que fa a la sanitat pública es garanteixen les urgències i els tractaments inajornables i la resta de serveis funcionen com un dia festiu. Així, en el cas de l’atenció primària els serveis mínims asseguren un 25 % de la plantilla habitual en els serveis no urgents.
